title: Creatures
build: Thalamus's two-sided disk release, G64 images of side A (SHA-256 4544cf5d…) and side B (b30bb735…) from the C64 Preservation Project's collection; the title says 1990, the collection 1991 (orientation.md)

records.c: Eight sprite shapes, 64 bytes each, for the high-score name entry: memory_swap 9 exchanges $E000-$E1FF with $6000-$61FF (sprite blocks $80-$87) as the entry starts ($E2C4) and ends ($E349). $80 and $81 are the left and right halves of the blue pool (sprites 6 and 7, doubled in both directions), $82 a grey rock (sprite 5) and $83-$87 frames of the fuzzy in the pool (sprite 4, pool_frames).
One more frame of the pool's fuzzy, 64 bytes: name_sprites_swap exchanges it with sprite block $88 at $6200 for the name entry, so that frame $88, the last of pool_frames, shows it.

The high-score name entry, which the engine calls ($C954) after the last life while this block is in. hiscore_check finds the score's place; with none (carry set) it goes straight back to the engine at $C957 through $E506. Otherwise it turns the character set the right way up if its blank character reads as set ($5FF8), prints "YOU'RE IN THE TOP 8" in big letters at $4403, starts the name as "....", draws the 40 heart_symbols round the heart from $452B, builds the cursor's box in sprite block $0F, swaps in its sprites (memory_swap 9, name_sprites_swap), places the pool and its creatures, puts the cursor on the first symbol (heart_start), plays the tune at $FC85 and starts its pair of raster routines at $E49D. Then name_loop, once a frame.
$27 into the selection $1220 (the cursor on the first symbol, the one after the last), fire_up_latch and $122B.

The name entry's sprites: sprite multicolours dark grey and yellow, pointers from name_sprite_frames, colours from name_sprite_colours, sprites 1-7 placed from name_sprite_xy; sprites 1, 2, 6 and 7 doubled both ways and 3 in width, multicolour for sprites 4 and 5, all behind the characters and all on; $122A, $1228 and $1229 set for name_pool_step.

The name entry's main loop, once a frame, until the name is finished ($1226 set by name_fire). Then it blanks the screen, turns the character set back, silences the sound, clears the screen, swaps the sprites back, copies the four characters into hiscore_names at the place hiscore_check found (zpa_84, four times the place), any $40 as $FF, clears the sprite blocks and returns to the engine at $C957.

Each frame of the entry: the cursor sprite to $1259/$125B; on alternate frames four colour lists turn (rotate_bytes 7, 8, 6 and 5); then heart_colours is laid round the heart from $D92B, so that the colours run round it.

Joystick 2 left or right moves the selection $1220 one symbol round the heart, at once and then every sixth frame while held ($121F), wrapping between 0 and $27; the cursor is put back on the first symbol and stepped round to the symbol after the selection. With neither, fire (fire_pressed) takes the symbol (name_fire).

The symbol under the cursor written into the name (name_char_from_cursor); the cursor's colour from heart_colours, 14 places on; the name's two rows cleared; colours for the two top rows (title_top_colours) and the name's rows (title_bottom_colours).

Centres the name: counts the wide letters (M, W) in $1222 and the narrow ones (I, '.', the apostrophe) in $1223, then moves the name's start one column left for each two wide and right for each two narrow from $477F, the column kept in the operand at $E48E. With a count below two the loop runs 256 times, which changes nothing.
Prints the name (print_big string $12, name_buffer) at $47xx, moves the pool's creatures (name_pool_step) and plays the music, then the next frame.
Operand of the LDX at $E48D: the low byte of the name's screen address, $7F less the wide letters' columns and plus the narrow ones'.

Raster routine at line $D4 for the name entry: adds one to the frame flag and sets $D016 to $CC, scrolling the screen four pixels right, so that the top line and the name sit centred between two columns. Next: $E4AC at line $4C.
Raster routine at line $4C: $D016 back to $C8, no scroll, for the heart. Next: $E49D at line $D4.

The nine initials of the slogan "CLYDE RADCLIFFE EXTERMINATES ALL THE UNFRIENDLY REPULSIVE EARTH-RIDDEN SLIME", as offsets from row 6, column 4: 0, 6, $10, $1D, $2C, $30, $3B, $57, $64. They spell CREATURES, and the opening scene colours them from title_top_colours ($ECD8).

The print_at string for each of the seven credit lines, printed from the last (credit_step): $0F-$15, the slogan's three lines, "AN APEX COMPUTER PRODUCTION", the programmer, the graphics and sound, and "COPYRIGHT THALAMUS 1990".
The high byte of each credit line's screen address.
21 bytes, seven rows of a sprite shape that title_swap copies into sprite block $0D at $435E: the small cloud the opening scene's sky sprites show.
21 bytes that nothing reads: the same bytes as the witch's shop file at these addresses (the end of its layout_witch and its potion colours), left over when this file was made.

JMP level_enter: the first of this block's three entries. The engine jumps here ($BE5F) once level 1.1's file has loaded, and the game begins at the title; for every later level the witch's shop sits here instead.
JMP $C91F: the engine's way back after the last life (game_end, $1CD4, and $BE62) and after the ending, through level_enter's second entry, which runs the name entry.
JMP $C957: back to the engine's title set-up after the name entry, whether or not a name was entered.

The frames of the fuzzy in the pool, one every four steps of name_pool_step ($47FC, sprite 4's pointer), ended by 0: $84, eight $85s, $86 and $87 in turn with $85s between, $84, eleven $83s, and $88. At the end frame $88 is held for $122B steps (39, then 40 each round), the splash is hidden, and the list starts again from its 33rd byte: ten $83s and the $88.

The pool's show, about ten seconds into the entry ($1228 counts 255 steps of two frames). First the two black expanded sprites 1 and 2, in front of the pool's sprites, slide apart one pixel every other frame until sprite 1 is at x $5C, opening on the pool; then, after $1229's 200 steps, sprite 4 takes the next of pool_frames every fourth step. While sprite 4 shows frame $88, every third frame sprite 3 is put at y $7F and given the next of four splash shapes (splash_lo/hi) in sprite block $0D.
Operand of the LDA at $E5C0 (two bytes): the splash shape being copied, from splash_lo/hi.
High byte of the LDA's operand at $E5C0. The splash shape's 21 bytes go to $4349, rows 3-9 of sprite block $0D.

Two colour lists of 20 (rotate_bytes lists 7 and 8, turned opposite ways in the name entry), read together as 40 colours for the name entry's two top rows ($E437): black, blue, purple, light blue, cyan, light green, white, then yellow, light grey, light red, orange, brown, black and the same back. The opening scene turns list 7 and colours the slogan's initials from its first nine ($ECD8).

Writes the code of the symbol after the selection (heart_symbols, Y = $1220 + 1, the one the cursor stands on) into name_buffer at position $1221, in the form print_big takes: letters to ASCII (the one after Z comes out as $5B, which print_big draws as 0), the digits, '.' and the apostrophe, $3F for the rub sign, $40 for the end sign, and A again after the end.

Fire on a symbol. The end sign fills the rest of the name with $3F and sets $1226, finishing the entry. The rub sign clears the position ('.', or the end mark in the fifth place), steps back one and shows the cursor's symbol there. Any other symbol moves on a place; after the fourth, the selection goes to the end sign ($1220 = $26, the cursor sprite to x $A3, y $61).
The low bytes of the four splash shapes, 21 bytes each: $E6AB, $E696, $E681, $E6C0, read from the end.
Their high bytes, all $E6.
Four shapes of seven sprite rows each (21 bytes), from $E681 to $E6D4: small drops that sprite 3 shows over the pool.
The third splash shape from its 19th byte, and the fourth.
The name entry's sprite pointers: the cursor ($0F), the two black blocks that cover the pool ($0E), the splash ($0D), the fuzzy ($83), the rock ($82) and the pool's halves ($80, $81).
Their colours: black for the first three, light blue, light red twice, and blue for the pool.
The x and y of sprites 1-7 (14 bytes): the black blocks and the pool's halves at ($84, $76) and ($B4, $76), the splash at ($A8, $7F), the fuzzy at ($B5, $7F) and the rock at ($9F, $7F).
Exchanges pool_frame_88 with sprite block $88 at $6200 and fills block $0E ($4380) with $FF, a solid block.

Exchanges the opening scene's 160 bytes of characters ($F023, title_chars) with characters $3B-$4E at $59D8, copies cloud_shape_rows into sprite block $0D, and exchanges walker_shape with sprite block $88. Called as the title starts and again before a game, so each time it puts the other set in place.
Sets the sprite registers from set X of the tables below: multicolour 1 and 2, priority, multicolour, expansion in x and y, the x high bits and the enable bits.
CE BF B7, the instruction DEC $B7BF: title_start writes it back over $1CA0, undoing the cheat.

The title, entered from the engine's title set-up ($C978). Turns the character set, swaps in the title's characters and shapes (title_swap), sets the scene timers and the first scene (opening_scene_setup), puts back the fuzzies' face and colour (10, light red) and the DEC $B7BF at $1CA0 that the cheat replaces, arms timing_check, plays the title tune and starts the raster chain at $E828. Then the title loop.
Operand of the STA at $E7A2 (two bytes): $1CA0, where dec_lives_bytes go, set and then spoiled again to $FFFF.

High byte of the STA's operand at $E7A2. After the copy, arms timing_check, turns extended colour and multicolour off, plays the title tune (music_play $CA2D) and starts the raster chain at $E828 with $01 = $35.

Waits for the frame flag. Fire starts a game: blanks the screen, black border and silence, clears the screen, swaps the title's characters and shapes back (title_swap), clears sprite blocks, memory swaps 6 and 10, game_new, and the Get Ready screen. Otherwise, when the scene's time ($1238) runs out, it switches between the opening scene (opening_scene_setup) and the high-score page (hiscore_page) by $121D.

Raster routine at line $F0, the title's first: border and background in the colour at $E829, timing_check (while logo_lines is 1), frame_divider, music_frame, and the high-score fuzzies' phases (fuzzy_phase_times into $125A and $F6AE). Adds one to the frame flag. In the opening scene ($120C = 0) it goes on to opening_scene_raster; while a page is being drawn ($120C = 1) it ends there; on the high-score page it reads the cheat once the tune has ended (title_cheat_input) and moves the page on.
Operand of the LDA at $E828: the border and background colour, 0 on the high-score page and 14 (light blue) in the opening scene.

The high-score page, each frame once $120E has run down: logo_lines falls by one a frame from $AC to $0A, so that the table rises into place, with colour_waves on its lines while the count is below $A0. Then the count goes to 1 and the logo is shown: the eight logo sprites at y $34 (logo_sprites, logo_colours), behind a top band of character $4F that dissolves a step every fifth frame (wipe_step). heart_colours turns on alternate frames, and $1238 counts down every fourth.

Raster routine at line $2A of the high-score page: for logo_lines lines it rewrites $D011's fine scroll on every line from $D012's low bits (EOR $1C), so that no character row can start (a flexible line distance): the table below is pushed down by that many lines. The loads and the CMP ($01,X) between are timing. Then, on alternate frames, colour list 4 turns into two rows ($D8CD, $D8F5) with title_row_colour. Next: fuzzies_raster at line $60 once the count is below $0A, otherwise $E828 at $F0.
Operand of the LDX at $E8D6: the lines the table is pushed down, $AC when the page starts, down to $0A, then 1.
Ends the chain for the frame: $E828 next, at line $F0.
Four sprite sets for sprite_set (X 0-3), one byte each in the eight tables that follow: sprite multicolour 1, $0A, $0B, 0, $0B.
Sprite multicolour 2 for each set: 7, 7, 0, 7.
Sprite priority for each set: 0, then $FF (all behind the characters).
Sprite multicolour bits for each set: $FF, $FF, 0, $FF.
Sprite x expansion for each set: 0, 0, $39, 0.
Sprite y expansion for each set: $FF for set 0, then 0.
The x high bits for each set: $80 for set 0.
Set 1's x high bits: 2 at the start (the second walker's x above 255), cleared by the opening scene when that walker crosses 256.
Set 2's x high bits, flipped bit by bit by clouds_raster as each cloud crosses x 0.
Set 3's x high bits, $66.
The enable bits for each set: $FF.

Sets up the opening scene ($120C = 1 while drawing): clears the screen, multicolour on, draws three rows of grass ($3B, $3C and $3D at $4770, $4798 and $47C0, coloured light green, light grey and orange), fills the sky (rows 0-17) with character $4F in light blue and makes $4F a full block (wipe_char_set 7), so that the sprites behind it are hidden; sets the timers ($1238 $87, $122F $32), the walkers at their start, the fuzzy poses (index $1215 9), the credit lines (7), the logo above the screen (y 2), $1240 9 and $EC2C $18, then $120C = 0.
The border colour at $E829 to 14, light blue.
Sets the y of all eight logo sprites in logo_xy to A.

How each of the eight cloud sprites moves, read from the end by clouds_raster: $FF a pixel every fourth frame, 0 every other frame, 1 every frame, 2 one and two pixels in turn. The eighth (Y 7) is the first byte of cloud_colours, 0.
The clouds' sprite colours for sprites 0-7, read from its second byte by $ED29: white and light grey.
The x and y of the eight cloud sprites, 16 bytes; clouds_raster moves the x's left.
The x and y of the eight logo sprites, from sprite 0's x ($58): logo_sprites copies them to $D000-$D00F. Each y is logo_y's.
Sprite 0's y in logo_xy, then the other sprites' x and y: the x's run from $70 in steps of $18, so the eight sprites side by side make the logo.
The logo's sprite frames, $80-$87, with a leading byte: logo_sprites reads them at $EA41-$EA48.
The logo's moves as it lands, read from the end of 24 steps: a value with bit 7 set moves it up by the low bits, others down, so that it bounces and settles.
Nine bytes, the first a filler: the top logo's sprite colours ($EC12). They start black, and $ED3C moves a white one along them.
The top logo's eight sprite colours from the second byte of logo_glint.
48 colours that rotate_bytes turns as list 9 on alternate frames once the credits are up: black, the greys, yellow, white and light green in bands. 34 of them colour credit row 10 ($D993).
colour_list_9 from its seventh byte, for credit row 13 ($DA0B).
Inside colour_list_9. The label is the engine's: its $1111 jumps to the KERNAL's $EA7E with the ROM banked in.
48 colours turned as list 10 on the other frames; 34 colour credit row 15 ($DA5B).
colour_list_10 from its seventh byte, for credit row 12 ($D9E3).

The colour list colour_waves turns as list 11 and copies into the high-score table's first, third, fifth and seventh lines (rows 8, 12, 16 and 20, two rows each), reading at $EACC, $EACE, $EAD0 and $EAD2, so that each line is two colours behind the last: bands of purple, red, orange, light red, yellow, white, light green, cyan, green, light blue, purple, dark grey and blue, repeated.
colour_waves_a from its third byte.
colour_waves_a from its fifth byte.
colour_waves_a from its seventh byte.
The second list of colour_waves (list 12), for the table's even lines (rows 10, 14, 18 and 22), read at $EAFC, $EAFE, $EB00 and $EB02 on the other frames.
colour_waves_b from its third byte.
colour_waves_b from its fifth byte.
colour_waves_b from its seventh byte, the same bands as colour_waves_a.

The credit lines' text, each ended by $FF: "CLYDE RADCLIFFE EXTERMINATES ALL", "THE UNFRIENDLY REPULSIVE", "EARTH-RIDDEN SLIME", "AN APEX COMPUTER PRODUCTION", "PROGRAMMING   : JOHN ROWLANDS", "GRAPHIX, SONIX : STEVE ROWLANDS", "COPYRIGHT THALAMUS 1990" (print_at strings $0F-$15), to $EBEA.
Sprite multicolours 1 and 2 for the logo, from heart_colours' entries 9 and 27, so that the logo's colours move with the list.
Moves the wipe character on a shape (wipe_char_set with $1230 + 8) until $1230 reaches $4F; returns with N set once it has.

The opening scene's work at line $F0. Puts all eight sprites at y $32 with their colours from logo_glint, so that the logo also shows at the top of the next frame, all behind the characters, with the logo's multicolours, and waits for the raster to pass the top of the screen. Then, once the logo has landed ($EC2C no longer $18), opening_scene_step, the credits and their colours.
Operand of the LDA at $EC2B: $18 until the logo has landed, then the bounce's last count (1). While it is $18, opening_scene_step runs from $ED76 instead and this routine goes on at line $18.

The credits: after $122F frames, every sixth frame the sky's character dissolves a step (wipe_step), showing the clouds and the top logo behind it, and with each of the first steps the next slogan row is coloured blue ($D8F5, $D921, $D94C); $1238 counts down.

Once the sky is clear: on alternate frames colour lists 9 and 10 turn into the rows at $D993/$DA0B and $D9E3/$DA5B; list 7 turns and the slogan's initials take their colours (slogan_initials); and every 16 frames the next credit line is printed (credit_step).
Prints credit line $1233 - 1 (credit_strings, credit_rows_hi/lo) every 16 frames, from the slogan's first line down to the copyright.
Next: $ED12 at line $60.

Raster routine at line $60 of the opening scene, between the two logos. Once $122F has run out: the eight cloud sprites from cloud_xy, all frame $0D, colours from cloud_colours, sprite set 2; and on alternate frames the glint moves on (logo_glint[$1240] black, the next white, $1240 stopping at 8). Next: $ED76 at line $AF.
Next: $ED76, at the line in A.
The logo: the eight sprites' positions from logo_xy, frames $80-$87 (logo_frames), all sprite colours black, then sprite set X.

Raster routine for the logo, at line $18 while it falls and $AF once it has landed: logo_sprites, its multicolours from heart_colours, and, while the raster is still in the top half, opening_scene_step. Next: walkers_raster at line $C8.

The opening scene's frame. heart_colours turns on alternate frames. Once $120E has run down, the walkers step every frame: the first right until x $7F, the second left (its high bit cleared as it passes 256), with frames from the level's tables at $A586 and $A577, a new pair every fourth frame. When the first has stopped, every 21 frames ($1213) the next of fuzzy_poses is drawn in characters (fuzzy_pose_draw), until $1214 is set. Then the logo falls 14 lines a step until y $B9 and bounces (logo_bounce, $122D steps), the fuzzies squashed under it (pose 4).
The BEQ that skips the walkers' frames except on every fourth frame. The label is the engine's: its drive code calls the KERNAL's TKSA at $EDC7 with the ROM banked in.
The second walker's frame into $F721. The label is the engine's: its drive code calls the KERNAL's CIOUT at $EDDD with the ROM banked in.

While the cell at $472D holds a pose's character (bit 7 clear) the walkers show the blank frame $0F, so that the fuzzies drawn in characters stand in their place; while it holds the blank $FF (pose 3) they show frame $D1.
LDA #$0F, hidden in the BIT at $EE12. The label is the engine's: its drive code calls the KERNAL's ACPTR at $EE13 with the ROM banked in.
The logo's fall, once the poses are done ($1214) and before the bounce: 14 lines a step until y $B9; then, with the last pose still drawn, pose 4 (the fuzzies squashed) and the bounce.
The bounce: $122D counts 24 steps, each moving the logo by logo_bounce; at the last, $EC2C takes the count.
Operand of the SBC at $EE66: the bounce's upward move.
Sets the logo's y (logo_y).

Raster routine at line $C8. Before the poses are done, the walkers: sprites 0 and 1 from walker_xy and walker_frames, mid grey, sprite set 1; afterwards a matching delay instead (nop_slide twice). Then multicolour characters, background colours 1 and 2 dark grey and mid grey for the top row of grass. Next: clouds_raster at line $E2.

Raster routine at line $E2: background colours 1 and 2 brown and light red for the lower rows of grass, then moves the eight clouds left by cloud_speeds, flipping a cloud's bit in clouds_x_msb as its x passes 0; one that leaves on the left comes back at x $1F7, and the fourth one doing so starts the glint again ($1240 = 0). Ends the chain ($E923).
Operand of the SBC at $EEE1: this sky sprite's step, 0, 1 or 2.

Draws pose X of the two fuzzies in characters: three characters of each fuzzy's top row at $472D and $4739, three of the bottom at $4755 and $4761, from fuzzy_pose_left_lo/hi and fuzzy_pose_right_lo/hi.

Draws the high-score page ($120C = 1 while drawing): clears the screen, makes character $4F a full block again, black border and background, hires characters; prints the eight places, each place and score and then the name, in big letters (hiscore_line, print_big strings 2 and 3) two rows apart from row 8; prints "TODAYS TOP HEROS" (string 4) at $44CD; fills the top five rows and the side columns with character $4F, black blocks that hide the logo and the fuzzies (sprites behind the characters) until wipe_step dissolves them; sets logo_lines to $AC, $120E $32 and $120F 0, sprites off, then $120C = 2.
The side columns of rows 8-23, columns 1-4 and 35-39, filled with character $4F.
The RTS that ends hiscore_page; title_swap counts from here, so its first byte is never moved.
160 bytes, the opening scene's characters $3B-$4E (the grass rows and the fuzzies drawn in characters), exchanged with $59D8 by title_swap.
The wipe character's shapes, eight bytes each, that wipe_char_set copies into character $4F: a full block, then diamonds that shrink, to $F102.
The last two wipe shapes: a single dot, then nothing (to $F112).
title_cheat_input's state: 0 waiting for the 2 key, 1 waiting for CTRL, 2 waiting for 2 again.
Frames since the last key of the cheat; ten or more starts it again.
Pairs of keys so far; at 30 ($1E) the cheat is in.
The fuzzies' frame for each state of the cheat: $4E, $4F, $4E, so that the fuzzies turn as the keys come in.
The infinite-lives cheat, read once a frame on the high-score page after the title tune has ended ($E871): title_cheat_step, then the fuzzies' frame from cheat_faces.

Reads keyboard row 7, which keyboard_release leaves selected ($DC00 = $7F): bit 3 of $DC01 is the 2 key, bit 2 CTRL (or joystick 1's right and left). The keys must come in turn, 2, CTRL, 2, each within ten frames; after 30 pairs it writes three NOPs over the DEC $B7BF at $1CA0, so that losing a life takes none, and makes the fuzzies mid grey ($F6E3 = 12). Holding CTRL and 2 together does it, since the state changes every frame.
RTS. The label is the engine's: the KERNAL's GETIN, called by the engine with the ROM banked in.
The cheat: $EA (NOP) written to $1CA0-$1CA2 through the STA at $F193, its operand set and then spoiled to $FFFF, and the fuzzies' colour to 12.
Operand of the STA at $F193 (two bytes): $1CA0 while the NOPs are written.
High byte of the STA's operand at $F193. After the NOPs are written the operand is spoiled to $FFFF again and the fuzzies' colour at $F6E3 set to 12; then the cheat's state and count are cleared.
83 bytes to $F1FF that nothing reads: the same bytes as the witch's shop file at these addresses (its witch_low_frames, witch_low_colours and leftover_F1BD), left over when this file was made.
